summary: Array methods add, remove, replace, and search items. Use them when the number of items changes while the program runs.
notes: push() adds to the end. unshift() adds at the front and shifts everything else right.
pop() removes and returns the last item. shift() removes and returns the first.
splice(index, 1) removes one item at that index. There is no remove-by-value method, so find the index first.
pitfall: playlist.splice(playlist.indexOf("Hello"), 1) on a missing value removes the last song with no error, because indexOf() returns -1 and splice(-1, 1) counts from the end.
contrast: A JavaScript array grows and shrinks like a Python list, so there is no separate ArrayList as in Java. The names differ: push() instead of append(), and splice() removes by index because there is no remove-by-value method.
